messages:
Evan: hey all, first week! trying to bring up local stack with docker-compose. postgres container exits with `could not create listen socket: Address already in use`. compose still shows container as exited. app errors with \"connection refused\". i'm on macbook (homebrew postgres also installed). anyone have quick tips?
Nora: welcome Evan :wave: that error usually means your host already has something listening on 5432 (likely your Homebrew Postgres). run `brew services list` or `pg_ctl -D /usr/local/var/postgres status` to check.
Evan: `brew services list` shows postgresql started. i didn't realize it auto-started. what are my options without uninstalling it?
Diego: you can either stop the host service (`brew services stop postgresql`) so the container can bind 5432, or change the compose port mapping to another host port like `5433:5432` and update your local env to point to that port. both are fine for dev.
Evan: tried `brew services stop postgresql` and then `docker-compose up postgres`  the container now stays up! logs: \"database system is ready to accept connections\". thanks.
Evan: quick follow up: tests still fail complaining about socket file `/tmp/.s.PGSQL.5432` not found when app uses default connection string. i'm setting DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pass@localhost:5432/redwood_dev locally.
Nora: macOS libpq can prefer unix sockets when you pass `localhost`. When you use `localhost`, some clients try a socket first. Try `127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost` in DATABASE_URL to force TCP: `postgres://postgres:pass@127.0.0.1:5432/redwood_dev`.
Diego: also note if you mapped to 5433: `postgres://postgres:pass@127.0.0.1:5433/redwood_dev`.
Evan: switching to 127.0.0.1 fixed the socket error. tests now hit the DB but migrations failed because the compose was using a host bind mount for pgdata and initdb permissions error popped up. i had `- ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` in compose.
Nora: on mac we recommend named volumes instead of host bind mounts to avoid permission/uid problems. change to:
```
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:15
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: localpass
      POSTGRES_DB: redwood_dev
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - \"5432:5432\"

volumes:
  pgdata:
```
Diego: if you did `brew services stop` earlier and want to keep host Postgres around, prefer changing compose to `5433:5432` instead so no one needs to stop their Homebrew service.
Evan: updated to named volume and re-ran `docker-compose up -d`. waited for healthcheck and ran `./dev/setup-db.sh`. migrations/seeds applied and test suite passes :tada:. added notes to my onboarding checklist about the brew conflict and `127.0.0.1` tip.
setup-bot: FYI: onboarding checklist item added: \"If you run Homebrew Postgres, stop it or change compose port to avoid 5432 conflict\"
DevEx: thanks Evan, i'll drop a one-liner in the README about preferring `127.0.0.1` in DATABASE_URL for host-based dev to avoid unix-socket confusion and a paragraph about named volumes on mac.
Evan: super helpful, appreciate the quick assist :heart:
